stories.headline: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
stories.summary: I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser.
stories.why_it_matters: But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: As the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants.
Technical Implementation: Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.
Deployment & Impact: Because this data is so valuable to Tau, the company charges less for cleaning than one might expect for such a cutting-edge product.

stories.headline: Our Response To The eMudhra Key Disclosure Incident
stories.summary: The Go Blog Our Response To The eMudhra Key Disclosure Incident Roland Shoemaker, on behalf of the Go Security team 26 October 2026 On October 19, the Go team initiated an expedited security release to protect Go users and their applications from a critical public key infrastructure (PKI) compromise involving certificates issued by eMudhra. Within approximately seven and a half hours of being notified, we shipped a targeted patch, which was included in our first-ever URGENT track security release.
stories.why_it_matters: Here is the context behind the incident, why Go stepped in at the runtime level to protect our users and how our incident response unfolded. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.

stories.headline: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
stories.summary: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5).
Technical Implementation: The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull.
Deployment & Impact: Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived.

stories.headline: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing
stories.summary: Serdar Cellat , Yuchen Xie , Bernadette Marcu , Blaid Burgess , Cody Jarrett , Carlos Pereira , Qing Shi , Samuel Carvajal , Manuel Pamplona , Dorothy Jung , Feiko Ritsema , Benjamin Klein , Alex Woo , Eugene Lok , Anna Pulido , Rebecka Swe , Sanford Holsapple , Ranjith Kumar Shetty Introduction Clips in the Netflix mobile app. At Netflix, a crucial part of our mission is ensuring our content looks stunning on any device.
stories.why_it_matters: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Traditionally, creating vertical assets meant editors and producers manually reframed horizontal videos in editing tools, a process that doesn’t scale as our catalog and use cases grow.

Technical Implementation: To support both our in‑app feed and external marketing campaigns at scale, we built an automated multi‑ratio video cropping system, tightly integrated into our internal production tools, that can generate high‑quality vertical and other aspect‑ratio variants with minimal manual effort.

Deployment & Impact: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app.

stories.headline: KDASO: Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization for Liability Adjudication Tasks
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.06972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liability adjudication tasks (e.g., legal charge determination) require analyzing event descriptions against domain-specific skills to determine whether a party should bear liability. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in this area by leveraging executable skills for interpretable reasoning, existing approaches face three critical limitations: skill libraries become stale as real-world scenarios dynamically evolve, skill descriptions often suffer from a semantic execution gap where LLMs deviate from intended expert logic, and growing skill collections exceed context budgets causing critical skill omission.
stories.why_it_matters: To address these challenges, we propose Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization (KDASO), which continuously evolves a skill library through neighborhood-conditioned induction from recent adjudication data, execution-aligned refinement based on LLM trajectory analysis, and context-budgeted routing for scalable skill selection. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in this area by leveraging executable skills for interpretable reasoning, existing approaches face three critical limitations: skill libraries become stale as real-world scenarios dynamically evolve, skill descriptions often suffer from a semantic execution gap where LLMs deviate from intended expert logic, and growing skill collections exceed context budgets causing critical skill omission.

Technical Implementation: To address these challenges, we propose Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization (KDASO), which continuously evolves a skill library through neighborhood-conditioned induction from recent adjudication data, execution-aligned refinement based on LLM trajectory analysis, and context-budgeted routing for scalable skill selection.

Deployment & Impact: KDASO further achieves 8.96% improvement when transferring skills to concept-similar scenarios and maintains consistent performance gains through continuous optimization, underscoring the high transferability and stability of generated skills.

stories.headline: One Word, Two GPUs: Why Gemma 4 Answers the Same Question Differently on a Laptop and a Tesla T4
stories.summary: Same GGUF file, same llama.cpp build, greedy decoding, and a GTX 1650 Ti answers $20 where a Tesla T4 answers 2000. One GSM8K question followed down to the word where the two cards part, the order in which each card adds its numbers, and the one stock setting that makes them agree.
stories.why_it_matters: Significantly impacts developers workflows, altering how developers deploy and maintain scalable software architectures.
